items.title: What GGLearn is and how you move through it
items.body: GGLearn is a training academy. You learn in tracks: each track is one subject, product, service, tool, technology or process. Every track has 20 levels, named from Novice (level 1) up to Titan (level 20). To pass a level you sit an exam that asks up to 10 questions and you need 80% to pass. Levels unlock in order. Before each exam there is a study guide with the level's syllabus and flip cards. Accounts are by invitation: a manager issues a single-use link tied to one email address and valid for 7 days. Passwords are 8 characters or more. A new person can be given required tracks with due dates; they appear on the dashboard under Required for you, and customers only ever see tracks made for customers.

questions.prompt: How many levels does every GGLearn track have?
questions.hint: Every track runs from level 1 (Novice) to level 20 (Titan).

questions.prompt: What is the first level of a track called?
questions.hint: Level 1 is Novice; level 20 is Titan.

questions.prompt: What is the top level of a track called?
questions.hint: Titan is level 20. Master (15) and Grandmaster (19) come before it.

questions.prompt: In GGLearn, what is a track?

options.text: One subject, product, service, tool, technology or process that you can learn and be tested on

questions.hint: A track is one area of knowledge with its own 20 levels.

questions.prompt: What score do you need to pass a level exam?
questions.hint: The pass mark is 80%.

questions.prompt: A level exam draws up to how many questions?
questions.hint: Each attempt draws up to 10 questions for that level.

questions.prompt: How do you get a GGLearn account?

options.text: You sign in with a social media account
Anyone can sign up on the home page
A manager sends you a single-use invite link for your email address

questions.hint: Signup is invite-only.

questions.prompt: Normally, what must you do before you can start level 6 of a track?

options.text: Nothing, any level can be taken at any time
Pass level 5 (or already be placed past it by the placement check)
Ask your manager to unlock it

questions.hint: Levels unlock in order.

questions.prompt: What does a study guide show you?

options.text: The level's syllabus and flip cards drawn from that level's questions

questions.hint: The study guide prepares you for the level before the exam.

questions.prompt: Where do you see the tracks you are required to pass, with due dates?

options.text: On your dashboard under Required for you

questions.hint: Required tracks and their deadlines are listed on the dashboard.

questions.prompt: How long is a GGLearn invite link valid, and how many times can it be used?

options.text: 30 days and any number of times

questions.hint: An invite is single-use, tied to one email, and valid for 7 days.

questions.prompt: Your invite link says it is not valid. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: It has expired or has already been used, so ask for a new one
Your browser is out of date

questions.hint: Invites expire after 7 days and work only once.

questions.prompt: You passed level 4 yesterday and want to sit level 6 today. What must you do?
questions.hint: Levels unlock in order.

questions.prompt: Why might the questions in your exam differ from your last attempt?

options.text: Questions change only once a year
Only your rival sees the same ones twice
Each attempt draws a fresh set of questions, favouring ones you have not yet answered correctly

questions.hint: Fresh draws mean you cannot just memorise one paper.

questions.prompt: Which tracks can a customer account open?

options.text: Only tracks they have paid extra for

questions.hint: Customer accounts only see customer-facing tracks.

items.title: Exams, levels and certificates
items.body: Multiple-choice answers are marked automatically against the answer key. Open and scenario answers are graded by Claude against a reference answer and rubric; without an AI key a coarse keyword fallback is used. Passing level 5, 10, 15 or 20 issues a certificate: level 5 is Foundation, level 10 Practitioner, level 15 Expert and level 20 Titan. Each certificate has a public code and can be verified at /cert/<code>. A failed exam can be retaken: the level stays locked and you try again with a fresh draw. The placement check is a short set of questions that finds the level you already know, so you start there instead of at level 1; it never places someone past level 15, higher levels have to be earned by exam.

questions.prompt: Which levels issue a certificate when you pass them?
questions.hint: Milestone levels 5, 10, 15 and 20 issue certificates.

questions.prompt: How are multiple-choice questions marked?

options.text: By a vote of other learners

questions.hint: Multiple-choice marking is automatic.

questions.prompt: What is the level-10 certificate called?
questions.hint: Foundation (5), Practitioner (10), Expert (15), Titan (20).

questions.prompt: How are open-answer questions graded?

options.text: Claude compares them with a reference answer and rubric, with a simpler keyword check if AI is unavailable
Only a manager can grade them

questions.hint: Open answers are marked against a reference answer and rubric.

questions.prompt: How can someone check that a certificate is genuine?
questions.hint: Every certificate has a public code that can be verified.

questions.prompt: What does the placement check do?

options.text: It finds the level you already know so you start there instead of level 1
It ranks you against everyone else

questions.hint: The placement check saves you repeating what you already know.

questions.prompt: You fail a level exam. What happens?

options.text: You are removed from the track
The level stays locked and you can try again with a fresh draw of questions

questions.hint: You can retake the exam; there is no lockout.

questions.prompt: What helps most when answering an open question?

options.text: Covering the key points a good answer should include
Writing as much as possible, whatever it says

questions.hint: Open answers are marked against a rubric of key points.

questions.prompt: You already know a subject well. What is the best way to avoid repeating the basics?

options.text: Take the placement check to start at a higher level

questions.hint: The placement check sets your starting level.

items.title: Daily quests, streaks and rivals
items.body: Each track has three daily quests: read the study guide (+20 XP), answer a five-question drill with instant feedback (+30 XP) and finish any level exam (+40 XP). Drills only draw from levels you have already passed, so they never reveal the exam you are about to sit; a brand-new learner drills level 1. A streak is the number of consecutive days, ending today or yesterday, on which you completed at least one quest. Every track has a stable, named rival who earns XP every day; on the scale used for rivals, 150 XP equals one level. The dashboard compares your levels with your rival's. Badges mark milestones such as passing your first level, a 3-day streak, a 7-day streak and earning a certificate.

questions.prompt: What is XP in GGLearn?

options.text: Experience points earned from quests and exams

questions.hint: XP measures your effort and feeds the race with your rival.

questions.prompt: Which three daily quests does each track offer?

options.text: Read the study guide, answer a five-question drill, finish an exam

questions.hint: Study guide, drill and exam are the three quests.

questions.prompt: What is a rival?

options.text: A named opponent assigned to each track who earns XP every day

questions.hint: A rival gives you someone to race on each track.

questions.prompt: What is the drill?

options.text: Five quick questions with instant feedback

questions.hint: The drill is short practice with immediate feedback.

questions.prompt: What does a streak count?

options.text: Consecutive days on which you completed at least one quest

questions.hint: Streaks reward showing up day after day.

questions.prompt: Which daily quest earns the most XP?
questions.hint: Exam +40, drill +30, study +20.

questions.prompt: Which levels can a drill draw questions from?

options.text: Only levels you have already passed
Only the exam you are about to sit

questions.hint: Drills never reveal the exam you are about to sit.

questions.prompt: On the scale GGLearn uses for rivals, how much XP equals one level?
questions.hint: A rival's level is its XP divided by 150.

questions.prompt: You completed a quest on Monday, then nothing on Tuesday or Wednesday. What is your streak when you open GGLearn on Thursday?

options.text: Zero: a streak needs consecutive days ending today or yesterday

questions.hint: The streak resets after a missed day.

items.title: Contests, privacy and your account
items.body: A contest is a time-boxed race on one track: gain a set number of levels (1 to 20) before a deadline of 1 to 90 days. Progress is growth, so beginners and experts race fairly. Ranking goes to who reached the goal first, then levels gained, then XP in the window. Contests can include simulated bots; a bot does not study or answer questions, it follows a fixed daily XP schedule and is labelled as simulated. A contest is private (only the organiser, invited people and members can open it) or public (anyone can watch, and joining requires consent that your name, photo and progress become public). A cash prize is optional: the organiser pays winners, GGLearn never holds or moves money. A profile photo is optional (JPEG, PNG or WebP up to 300 KB); colleagues who are signed in can see it and strangers see it only if you play in a public contest. Sign out everywhere ends your session on every device.

questions.prompt: Who can see your profile photo?

options.text: Signed-in colleagues, and strangers only if you play in a public contest

questions.hint: A photo is optional and its visibility is limited.

questions.prompt: You think you left yourself signed in on a shared computer. What should you do?

options.text: Use Sign out everywhere to end your session on every device

questions.hint: Sign out everywhere ends all your sessions.

questions.prompt: How long must a GGLearn password be?
questions.hint: Passwords are 8 characters or more.

questions.prompt: What photo can you upload to your profile?

options.text: A JPEG, PNG or WebP image up to 300 KB

questions.hint: Photos are optional and limited in type and size.

questions.prompt: What does a GGLearn contest measure?

options.text: Who answers fastest in one minute
Who gains the most levels in one track before the deadline

questions.hint: A contest is a race to gain a set number of levels.

questions.prompt: A contest offers a cash prize. Who pays it?

options.text: No one, prizes are not real
The organiser, because GGLearn never holds or moves money

questions.hint: Prize money is arranged between the organiser and winners.

questions.prompt: Who can open a private contest?

options.text: The organiser, invited people and members

questions.hint: Anyone else sees a not-found page.

questions.prompt: What do contest bots do?

options.text: Study and answer questions like a person
Follow a fixed daily XP schedule and are labelled as simulated

questions.hint: A bot does not actually study or answer questions.

questions.prompt: Who receives the champion certificate for a contest?

options.text: The best human who reached the goal

questions.hint: Champions and finishers are people who reached the goal.

questions.prompt: Your dashboard shows a required track as overdue. What should you do?

options.text: Work on it first, because required learning has a deadline

questions.hint: Overdue required learning is reported to managers.
